documents.title: Teaching with Generative AI
documents.summary: A teaching-center page presenting the 'Three Laws of Curriculum in the Age of AI' (teach about AI, teach with AI, protect learning) as a framework rather than a rule set. It cites Syllabus Policy #S25-257, which requires a syllabus statement on how and why generative AI can and cannot be used, and leaves the stance to faculty.
documents.stance_why: The page says 'Whatever your stance is with AI, CEETL recommends transparency' and the only binding rule it quotes is that faculty must state 'how and why generative AI tools can and cannot be used'; it sets no default and leaves the decision to instructors, so delegates.

units.why: CEETL states its own approach: AI as 'tools that may be used to enhance teaching and scholarship'. This is a principles preamble (P56) rather than a binding default, though it leans to P02.
